## Results

### HTF haplotype distribution and OBC status across eras

Four HTF haplotype groups were identified based on element length (HTF-1803, -1245, -1383, -1830), with HTF-1803 and -1245 carrying the O-antigen biosynthesis cluster (OBC+) and HTF-1383 and -1830 lacking it (OBC−). Within Historical isolates (n = 38), the four groups were nearly uniformly distributed (10 (HTF-1803), 11 (HTF-1245), 10 (HTF-1383), 7 (HTF-1830); chi-square goodness-of-fit chi2 = 0.95, df = 3, p = 0.814 [ns]), and OBC+ and OBC− strains occurred at near-equal frequencies (21/38 = 55.26% OBC+; exact binomial p = 0.627 [ns]; Wilson 95% CI: 39.7%–69.9%). In contrast, within Modern isolates (n = 1312), the four groups were strongly non-uniformly distributed (chi2 = 607.1, df = 3, p = 3.0 × 10⁻¹³¹ [***]), with OBC+ haplotypes predominating (1098/1312 = 83.69% OBC+; exact binomial p = 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁴³ [***]; Wilson 95% CI: 81.6%–85.6%).

### Cross-era shift in OBC status

The proportion of OBC+ isolates increased significantly from the Historical to the Modern era (Fisher’s exact test: OR = 0.241, p = 5.1 × 10⁻⁵ [***]). To account for the sample size imbalance (n = 38 vs. n = 1312), Fisher’s exact test was repeated using expected Modern counts scaled to n = 38 (OR = 0.236, p = 0.012 [*]), and confirmed by repeated random downsampling of n = 38 isolates from the Modern pool across 1000 draws (median p = 0.012; 85.2% of draws p < 0.05).

### Germany Historical subset

To compare without bias from sample size or geographic origin, Germany Historical isolates (n = 8) were extracted as the fixed reference group: 2 OBC+ (25%), 6 OBC− (75%). OBC− haplotypes predominated (6/8 = 75% OBC−; 2/8 = 25% OBC+), but this difference did not reach significance by exact binomial test (p = 0.289 [ns]; Wilson 95% CI for OBC+: 7.1%–59.1%), reflecting limited power at n = 8. A representative Modern group of n = 8 was then derived from the full Modern pool (1312 OTU5 isolates) by scaling the observed Modern OBC+ proportion to n = 8 (round(83.7% × 8) = 7 OBC+, 1 OBC−; Wilson 95% CI for OBC+: 49.0%–96.5%). Fisher’s exact test on this balanced 8 vs. 8 comparison confirmed a significant OBC− enrichment in Historical Germany (OR = 0.062, p = 0.041 [*]). Repeated random downsampling of n = 8 isolates from the full Modern pool across 1000 draws confirmed the robustness of this result (median Fisher p = 0.041; 61.2% of draws p < 0.05).

### Wilson 95% Confidence Intervals (lower panel Germany plots)

Wilson 95% confidence intervals for plotted OBC+ proportions were computed using `binom::binom.confint(k, n, method = "wilson")`. For the Modern representative, k = 6.695 (= Modern OBC+ proportion × 8, without rounding), centering the CI at the true Modern pool OBC+ proportion (83.7%) rather than the rounded integer count (7/8 = 87.5%). The floating k is used exclusively for CI computation and plot centering; all statistical tests (Fisher’s exact, binomial) use integer inputs.

| Group                            | n | k (OBC+) | OBC+ % | CI lower % | CI upper % |
|----------------------------------|---|----------|---------|------------|------------|
| Germany Historical               | 8 | 2        | 25.0    | 7.1        | 59.1 |
| Modern representative (n=8)      | 8 | 6.695    | 83.7    | 49.0       | 96.5 |

*Both `Oantigen_freq_Germany_hist_vs_resampleModern8.pdf` and `Oantigen_freq_Germany_simple_HvsM.pdf` use these CI values. The simple lower panel dot labels show the rounded integer proportion: 25% (2/8) for Historical and 87.5% (7/8) for Modern representative.*

## Methods

### Statistical tests

Within-era OBC+/− proportions were assessed by two-sided exact binomial test (H₀: p = 0.5). The distribution of all four HTF haplotype groups within each era was assessed by chi-square goodness-of-fit (H₀: 25% per group, df = 3). Cross-era differences in OBC status were assessed by Fisher’s exact test on 2 × 2 contingency tables (era × OBC status).

To address sample size imbalance between eras, two complementary approaches were applied for the Germany-specific comparison: (i) a balanced deterministic comparison — a representative Modern group of n = 8 was derived by scaling the observed Modern OBC+ proportion to n = 8 (round(83.7% × 8) = 7 OBC+), and Fisher’s exact test was run on the resulting 8 vs. 8 table; (ii) repeated random downsampling — 1000 draws of n = 8 without replacement from the full Modern OTU5 pool (n = 1312), with Fisher’s exact test applied to each draw against the fixed Germany Historical group; results are reported as the median p-value and proportion of draws with p < 0.05. The same balanced-downsampling framework (at n = 38) was applied for the full cohort cross-era comparison. Wilson 95% confidence intervals were computed using the binom R package. All analyses were performed in R (≥ 4.0). Significance thresholds: *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001.
